title: Card transactions with fraud flags, September 2026

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in night-time transactions
findings.detail: Night (0–5) has a 30.8% fraud rate on 718 rows, against 0.3% to 0.7% at other times. That is about 221 cases (718 × 30.8%), roughly 81% of the 272 total.

findings.headline: Online, digital goods and low-value payments carry the fraud
findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% rate (1,130 rows) and Online 6.3% (3,974 rows), against 0.3% to 0.5% for Contactless and Chip. The lowest amount band (up to 535.9) has an 11.4% rate against 0.3% to 0.6% elsewhere. These groups overlap, so do not add them up.

findings.headline: AE and SG transactions show very high fraud rates
findings.detail: AE has a 28.6% rate (206 rows) and SG 31% (187 rows), against 1.6% for IN. US and GB are 0.7% and 0.8%, so this is not a general overseas effect.

findings.headline: Weekly fraud rate rose sharply from early September
findings.detail: The rate went from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 1.7%, then 4.0% and 4.1% in the next two weeks. The last week is partial (727 rows) and shows 1.8%, so it is too early to call a fall.

findings.headline: Data is complete with no duplicates
findings.detail: All 10,260 rows have no missing cells and no duplicate rows. Transaction IDs are all distinct, so rates can be trusted as read. The data covers one month only.

next_steps: Review rules or step-up checks for night-time online digital goods payments, and test how many of the 272 fraud cases they would catch.
Check which of the AE and SG transactions are also night-time, online or digital goods, to see whether country adds anything on its own.
Find what changed around the weeks of 14 and 21 September, and re-run the weekly view once the 28 September week is complete.

reviews.note: 718 × 30.8% ≈ 221, and 221 ÷ 272 ≈ 81%. Other periods are 0.3% to 0.7%. Numbers and severity hold.
Rates match the summary. Changed 'carry the fraud' to 'is higher among' to avoid implying cause. Overlap caveat kept.
AE 28.6% (206 rows), SG 31% (187), IN 1.6%, US 0.7%, GB 0.8% all match. Every group is over 30 rows.
Weekly rates 0.6, 1.7, 4.0, 4.1, 1.8 match. Last week has 727 rows, so it is partial. Medium severity is fair.
Completeness figures are right, but complete data does not prove rates can be trusted as read. Removed that claim.

Test a step-up check or rule for night-time online digital goods payments on this data and count how many fraud cases it would catch.

conclusion: Fraud flags go with night-time activity, digital goods, online payments, small amounts and AE and SG transactions. Night-time alone accounts for roughly 81% of the 272 cases. First, check how far these groups overlap, so you act on the real drivers and not on the same transactions counted several times.
limits: This review uses summary statistics for one month, so it cannot show which factor matters on its own, why rates rose, or whether the fraud flags themselves are correct.
